Web search results for query: "CLI sync MCP servers config Claude Code Codex CLI Gemini CLI one file"

Links: [{"title":"mcp sync","url":"https://github.com/EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync"},{"title":"Crate mcp_sync","url":"https://docs.rs/mcp-sync/latest/mcp_sync"},{"title":"mcp sync","url":"https://github.com/ejfn/mcp-sync"},{"title":"github.com","url":"https://github.com/google/mcp-security/pull/186/files"},{"title":"sync agents settings","url":"https://proxy-ga.blitzz.co/proxy/123456/github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings"},{"title":"jnk234 mcp multiverse","url":"https://lobehub.com/zh/mcp/jnk234-mcp-multiverse"},{"title":"jnk234 mcp multiverse","url":"https://lobehub.com/mcp/jnk234-mcp-multiverse"}]

Several open-source tools do this. None of the results is an official, vendor-supported sync, and I didn't check their maintenance status or license.

- **ejfn/mcp-sync** is the closest match. It takes a Claude-format JSON file with a top-level `mcpServers` key as the source. It writes to Claude Code (~/.claude.json), Gemini CLI (~/.gemini/settings.json), VS Code, and Codex. For Codex, it notes that Codex only supports servers of type stdio. It also preserves existing servers in the target configs that aren't in the source unless you pass `--prune`.
- **sync-agents** (Leoyang183) treats Claude Code as the primary source. It can sync MCP server configurations and instruction files (CLAUDE.md) from Claude Code to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and several other tools. It also has a doctor command to check for config drift.
- **Crate mcp_sync** reads a single `mcp.yaml` and syncs the server definitions to configuration files for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. Gemini CLI isn't in its target list.
- **EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync** keeps one central file at ~/.config/mcp-sync/config.json, but its listed targets are Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, and Codex. Claude Code and Gemini CLI aren't in that list.

A no-tool option also appeared. A Google security PR notes that if you use multiple MCP clients, you can maintain a single config file and symlink it into each expected location. This only works if the client formats match, which they don't for Codex, since its config is TOML under `mcp_servers`.

The main takeaway is that ejfn/mcp-sync and sync-agents are the best fits for covering all three tools. Only ejfn/mcp-sync was described as covering Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex together.

content.content:
**MCP configs:** Yes, for all three, per the agent table:
- **Claude Code:** `.mcp.json`
- **OpenAI Codex CLI:** `.codex/config.toml`. To apply it, set `CODEX_HOME` to the project's `.codex` directory.
- **Gemini CLI:** `.gemini/settings.json`

**Merge/preserve:** The default MCP strategy is merge. `--mcp-overwrite` replaces the native config instead. Ruler also creates `.bak` backups of pre-existing agent config files it replaces, and backups are enabled by default. The page doesn't describe how merging handles every existing setting.

**Scope:** The page says "Ruler never writes MCP configuration files outside your project root."

**License:** MIT.

**Network calls:** The page doesn't say whether Ruler makes network calls in general. It does say that during OpenCode subagent generation, Ruler makes no network requests.

**Account:** Not mentioned.
